title: Presentation at Technical Committee on Service Computing (SC)｜Social Intelligence Laboratory, Ritsumeikan University
place: Location: The Kyoto College of Graduate Studies for Informatics
abstractContent: Mr.Matsumoto and Mr.Nakagawa gave a research presentation at the Services Computing Workshop and Mr.Matsumoto received the Young Scientist Incentive Award.

presentations.speaker: Kenji Matsumoto
presentations.title: API recommendation for service composition using large-scale language models
presentations.abstract: A new service built by linking multiple APIs is called a composite service. Composite services make it possible to provide expanded functions and added value that would be difficult to achieve with a single service. However, when building a composite service, it is extremely difficult to find the necessary APIs from the vast number of APIs. In this study, we propose a method to find a combination of APIs that meets requirements from a user's requirements statement written in natural language using the LLM prompting method. Specifically, we apply and evaluate the Few-Shot CoT method, which sets up an inference procedure for a generative AI, presents examples, and allows it to make inferences based on these.

presentations.speaker: Shinichi Nakagawa
presentations.title: Composite service recommendation using multi-layer multi-label classification
presentations.abstract: Composite service is a new service that combines multiple web services on the Internet. Service composition creates new services that users needs using existing web services. However, selecting the appropriate web services to construct a composite service that aligns with users needs is a challenging task.This study proposes a method that leverages a language model to determine appropriate service combinations based on user requirements expressed in natural language. The approach formulates the task as a multi-label classification problem and uses a pre-trained BERT model to solve it. Additionally, to improve selection accuracy, service categories are hierarchically structured, and a multi-layer multi-label classification model is applied.
